title: Method for Fabricating Self-Powered Cement Sensors Based on Gold Nanoparticles
author: Triana-Camacho, Ospina-Ospina, et al.

steps.title: Gather all required materials
steps.instruction: Collect a 30 mm diameter × 0.15 mm thick gold plate (99.9999 % purity), ultrapure water from a Milli‑Q IQ 7000 (18.2 MΩ), general‑use Portland cement (ARGOS Colombia), 2.5 mm copper desoldering wire (ref ZD‑180), PVC cylindrical molds (30 mm diameter, 60 mm height), mineral oil, silicon wafer (110 orientation), quartz cuvettes (1 mm path), and all instrumentation listed in later steps.

steps.title: Assemble pulsed laser ablation system
steps.instruction: Set up the Quantel Q‑smart 850 Nd:YAG laser (2ω, 532 nm) with Q‑Touch pad control, connect the c‑series energy‑meter console, mount the optical base and post holders, install the NB1‑K12 mirror to deflect the beam 90°, and place a beaker containing the gold target immersed in Milli‑Q water on the beam path.

steps.title: Synthesize gold nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Perform laser ablation at 25 °C with a laser spot area of 12.6 mm², pulse interval of 0.1 s, pulse duration of 8 ns, and pulse energy of 350 mJ. For low‑concentration Au NPs (442 ppm) use 10 mL water and ablate for 5 min; for high‑concentration Au NPs (658 ppm) use 50 mL water and ablate for 10 min. Measure the gold target mass five times on an Ohaus balance (readability 1 µg) before and after ablation to calculate the exact ppm. Additionally, run a two‑factor three‑level design varying water volume (5, 10, 20 mL) and laser energy (250, 300, 350 mJ) to target mean particle sizes between 100 nm and 500 nm.

steps.title: Measure nanoparticle size by DLS
steps.instruction: Ten minutes after ablation, transfer the Au NP dispersion into 1 mm optical‑path quartz cuvettes without dilution. Using an Anton Paar Litesizer 500, record the particle‑size distribution at a 90° detection angle. Perform each measurement in triplicate and average six series per test. Note that 5 min ablation yields d₅₀ ≈ 401 ± 33 nm (lower concentration) and 10 min ablation yields d₅₀ ≈ 77 ± 4 nm (higher concentration) with trimodal peaks at 2 nm, 25 nm, and 131 nm.

steps.title: Image Au NPs by SEM and UV‑Vis
steps.instruction: Drop the Au NP suspension onto a silicon wafer (110 plane) and dry on a heating plate at 60 °C until a thin film forms. Image the dried film with a FEI QUANTA FEG 650 SEM (25 kV, ETD SE detector, BSE SDD detector, resolution 126.1 eV Mn Kα). Use EDX Genesis software to confirm ~63 wt% Au. Acquire images at 500 nm, 1 µm, and 5 µm magnifications; the 500 nm image shows spherical particles with average size 110 ± 51 nm. Record UV‑Vis spectra in 1 mm quartz cuvettes on an Agilent 8453 spectrometer (deuterium and tungsten lamps); observe the Au NP plasmon peak at 511 ± 0.0003 nm.

steps.title: Hand‑mix cement paste with Au NPs
steps.instruction: Calculate a water‑to‑cement ratio (w/c) of 0.47 (average of two standard ratios). For each specimen weigh 60 g cement and add 28.2 g ultrapure water plus the required Au NP mass (0 mg for reference, 0.39 mg for 442 ppm, 0.58 mg for 658 ppm). Mix in a beaker until homogeneous; do not add any surfactant.

steps.title: Cast specimens in PVC molds
steps.instruction: Seal the interior of each 30 mm × 60 mm PVC cylinder with mineral oil. Pour the homogenized cement‑Au NP paste in three equal layers, compacting each layer by manual damping and placing the mold on a vibrating table for 10 min to reduce porosity.

steps.title: Embed copper wire electrodes
steps.instruction: Drill two 3 mm‑diameter holes in each mold at 1/3 and 2/3 of the total height. Insert the 3 mm‑wide copper desoldering wire (net thickness 0.05 mm) so that it lies flat as a plane inside the mold, establishing the two measuring electrodes separated by 20 mm.

steps.title: Cure specimens with or without electric field
steps.instruction: Unmold the specimens after 48 h of room‑temperature drying. Submerge them in ultrapure water for 28 days. For the electric‑field group, place the specimens between two copper plane electrodes (13 cm × 10 cm) oriented axially and apply a constant DC voltage of 20.5 V for the entire 28‑day curing period. After curing, heat all specimens in a furnace at 40 °C for 24 h. Label each specimen with a lowercase “p” followed by its fabrication sequence number (e.g., p10).

steps.title: Perform electrical impedance spectroscopy
steps.instruction: Connect each cured specimen to an AUTOLAB PGSTAT204 potentiostat/galvanostat (Nova 2.1 software). Apply an AC excitation of 10 mV and sweep the frequency from 1 MHz down to 100 mHz in 60 evenly spaced points. Save the impedance data for later fitting of Nyquist semicircles using the provided Python script semiCirclesEISModel().

steps.title: Run compressive test with OCP measurement
steps.instruction: Mount a specimen in an MTS‑Bionix universal testing machine (max 25 kN). Apply axial compressive load up to 2.0 kN at a constant rate of 0.02 kN s⁻¹ while simultaneously recording the open‑circuit potential (OCP) with the AUTOLAB potentiostat (no external voltage applied). Export the mechanical force and OCP data as .txt files.

steps.title: Analyze voltage‑force relationship
steps.instruction: Use the Python script pro_data() to import the OCP and force .txt files. Interpolate both time series to a common time base with the function plot_ocp_force(). Perform linear regression (V = γ F + β) to obtain the OCP‑mechanical coefficient γ (mV kN⁻¹) and the intercept β (V at zero force). Multiply γ by the electrode geometry factor (A/L) to calculate the piezoelectric voltage constant g₃₃ (10⁻⁵ mV m N⁻¹).
